Task: Analyze NDVI time series
Analyze vegetation dynamics in the ganzhe region using NDVI derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery for two time periods in 2020: January to August and August to December. Task: Map annual precipitation
Compute and visualizes the total accumulated precipitation for the year 2023 across the Brazilian state of Paraíba using CHIRPS daily rainfall data. It filters the CHIRPS ImageCollection for the date range '2023-01-01' to '2024-01-01', sums all daily images to produce a single annual precipitation raster, clips it to the administrative boundary of Paraíba (from FAO GAUL level-1), calculates min/max statistics over that geometry for visualization scaling, and overlays municipal boundaries (FAO GAUL level-2) for spatial reference. Task: Generate gap-filled NIRv time series
Generate a gap-filled, 8-day composite time series of the Near-Infrared Reflectance of Vegetation (NIRv) using MODIS MCD43A4 and MCD43A2 surface reflectance and quality data for the year 2004 over the high-latitude Northern Hemisphere. Task: Identify tree cover agreement
the workflow evaluates the agreement between a supervised land cover classification map and the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset's tree cover layer for the year 2000. Generate a median surface reflectance composite of Sentinel-2 imagery over Tunisia by masking clouds and their shadows using the QA60 band and geometric shadow projection. It computes mean VH backscatter across multiple time windows, stacks them into a multi-temporal raster, and clips the result to the district boundary. Additionally, it processes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from October 2021 and 2022 to generate false-color composites (B8, B4, B3) for visual interpretation of land cover. Outputs include two stacked SAR image composites (2021 and 2022), two optical mosaics (2021 and 2022), and their visualization layers on the map for comparative analysis of seasonal vegetation dynamics.

Task: Assess vegetation and water health
the workflow assesses temporal vegetation and water health in coastal Bangladesh using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery (2000–2024). It computes NDVI (B5/B4), NDWI (B3/B5), and an illustrative SPI (B2−B3); extracts annual maximum values over the ROI; generates time-series charts for NDVI and NDWI; and applies threshold-based classification to categorize pixels into 'Healthy', 'Moderate', or 'Unhealthy' for both vegetation (using NDVI thresholds: ≥0.6, ≥0.4, <0.4) and water (using NDWI thresholds: ≥0.3, ≥0.1, <0.1). Outputs include interactive time-series charts, max-value statistics, and classified image collections — all spatially constrained to Manikganj district (used as proxy for coastal districts despite comment mismatch), with no final raster export or area quantification implemented.
